target: no annotation for flower (PO_0009046), fruit or seed: they are unknown, not absent. The inflorescence (PO_0009049) obtriangular statement stands.

target: bract (PO_0009055): no whorled arrangement. The negation is of the arrangement, not of bracts. Bracts are sometimes present, scattered and lanceolate.
fix: 'whorls / rings / clusters / tufts of <part> absent' negates the arrangement, not the part. Do not emit '<part> absent'. A following 'but sometimes ...' clause marks the part as variably present.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039) absent only on the outer leaves (outer, FLOPO_0991379). The other leaves have acute blades.
fix: A series qualifier in front of the part (outer, inner, lower, lowest, basal, upper: config/flora_context_words.tsv bearer_quality) restricts an absence to that member. Annotate the absence on the qualified bearer, or drop it, but never on the part in general.
reason: In Aechmea the outer leaves are often reduced to bladeless sheaths. The blades of the main leaves are described as acute.

target: awn (PO_0025349) usually present. Awnless occurs only rarely (a frequency qualifier).
fix: 'rarely / sometimes / occasionally <part>-less' (or '... absent') describes a rare variant. Do not emit '<part> absent' for the taxon. Keep the presence, or mark the character as variable.
reason: 'rarely awnless' means that the awn is normally present, which agrees with the description of the awn's length.

target: spike inflorescence (PO_0030117) with the qualifier basal (FLOPO_0991002): absent. The terminal staminate (male, PATO_0000384) spike is present and sessile.
fix: 'basal <part> absent' restricts the absence to the basal members (FLOPO_0991002). Never annotate the plain part as absent. 'staminate' or 'pistillate' in front of a part likewise picks out a member.
reason: In Carex, 'basal spikes' are long-stalked spikes arising from the base. Their absence says nothing about the other spikes.

target: leaf lamina absent or nearly so only on the lower sheaths or leaves (lower, FLOPO_0991377), which is the usual Carex wording. The blades of the other leaves are stiff.
fix: 'bladeless or nearly so' is hedged. Emit no absence for it. If the subject that went before (lower sheaths, lowest leaves) has been lost, drop the statement rather than attaching it to the leaf lamina in general.
reason: Without its subject the phrase cannot be about all leaves, because blades are described elsewhere for the same taxon. Most likely it refers to the basal sheaths.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039) absent only in the lower leaves (lower, FLOPO_0991377), which are reduced to sheaths (PO_0020104). The other blades are light green.
fix: '<leaves> reduced to bladeless sheaths' -> those leaves have only a sheath. Restrict it to the leaves named or implied (lower or basal). It is never a whole-taxon 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: Carex descriptions typically read 'lower leaves reduced to bladeless sheaths'. The upper leaves have blades.

target: bract (PO_0009055) without a blade: the bracts are sheathing and bladeless. The leaf lamina (PO_0020039) is present: thick, light green.

target: leaf lamina absent only on the lowest leaves or sheaths (lowest, FLOPO_0991377). The blades of the other leaves are erect or ascending.

reason: A qualifier for one member of a series. The blades described belong to the other leaves.

target: bract (PO_0009055): the sheath is bladeless (Carex eburnea has sheathing bracts that are bladeless or nearly so). The foliage leaf lamina is present and roughened.
fix: 'the sheath bladeless' describes the sheath just mentioned (a bract sheath or a basal leaf sheath). Attach it to that sheath's owner, and never to the leaf lamina of the taxon in general.

target: leaf lamina absent only on the lower leaves or sheaths (lower, FLOPO_0991377). The other blades are roughened.

target: spike inflorescence (PO_0030117) with the qualifier basal (FLOPO_0991002): absent. The terminal staminate (PATO_0000384) spike is present, solitary and sessile.

target: blade absent only on the lower sheaths (lower, FLOPO_0991377; leaf sheath PO_0020104). The other leaves have yellowish-green blades.

target: drop 'stolon: length'. The sentence states only an absence: stolon (PO_0003024) absent, at least long horizontal ones. Nothing is measured.
